Counts, spacing, membrane thickness and cuts are teaching samples. Schwann covering and cleft basal-lamina samples are intentionally hidden here. Vesicles occupy the open nerve terminal; acetylcholine crosses the cleft to receptors on folds of the muscle-cell sarcolemma. The cleft is extracellular space, not a third cell.

Counts, spacing, membrane thickness and cuts are teaching samples. The repeating bands belong to intracellular myofibrils. A sarcomere spans Z disc to Z disc. The bands are regions defined by filament arrangement; they are not separate organelles.

SCHEMATIC 8 Filaments and overlap.note: SCHEMATIC: separate axial and transverse enlargement; biological measurements are unavailable. Counts, spacing, membrane thickness and cuts are teaching samples. Thin actin filaments insert at Z-disc anchoring lattices. Thick myosin filaments occupy the central A region; their overlap with thin filaments gives band organization. The central non-overlap H region lies inside A. The M line anchors the center; titin links thick filament to Z.

SCHEMATIC 9 Triad and membrane continuit.note: SCHEMATIC: separate axial and transverse enlargement; biological measurements are unavailable. Counts, spacing, membrane thickness and cuts are teaching samples. A T tubule is an inward extension of the sarcolemma, with extracellularly continuous lumen. Two SR terminal cisternae flank it near A–I boundaries. The SR network has a different lumen, and releases calcium into sarcoplasm during activation.

Counts, spacing, membrane thickness and cuts are teaching samples. The spindle is a length-sensitive sensory organ aligned with neighboring extrafusal fibers. Intrafusal fibers lie within its capsule. Its yellow central sensory ending differs from the motor end plate.
